Our Mission

 

Coventry University is a global education group committed to delivering impactful research that addresses major societal and industrial challenges. Our interdisciplinary research brings together academic expertise, advanced technologies and industry partnerships to develop practical solutions that support innovation, sustainability and economic growth.

 

As an ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally.

The Role

 

We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Research Fellow in Life Cycle Assessment and Techno-Economic Modelling to contribute to SUCCESSOR, a major European collaborative research project developing the next generation of sustainable, cost-effective lithium-ion batteries for electric mobility.

 

SUCCESSOR brings together leading academic and industrial partners to develop and scale up advanced lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP) battery technologies. The project aims to improve battery performance, manufacturing efficiency, environmental sustainability and economic competitiveness across the European battery value chain.

 

Working within Coventry University's Sustainable Manufacturing and Materials research activities, you will contribute to the environmental and economic evaluation of emerging battery technologies, with a particular focus on Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), industrial decarbonisation and techno-economic assessment (TEA).

 

You will develop and apply quantitative models to assess the environmental impacts, manufacturing costs and commercial feasibility of new materials and processes. Your research will help identify opportunities for sustainable industrial scale-up, supporting technology development and decision-making across the SUCCESSOR consortium.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

You will undertake independent and collaborative research across three closely related activities:

 

•    Industrial Decarbonisation and Resource Efficiency: Assess emissions reduction, resource efficiency and industrial symbiosis opportunities in battery manufacturing.
•    Life Cycle Assessment and Sustainability: Conduct life cycle assessments of emerging battery technologies across manufacturing and future deployment scenarios.
•    Techno-Economic Assessment: Develop techno-economic models to assess manufacturing processes, scale-up potential and commercial viability.

 

In addition, you will work collaboratively with industrial and academic partners to gather and analyse research data, communicate findings, contribute to project deliverables and produce high-quality academic publications.

Qualifications Required

 

A PhD, or equivalent professional research experience, in a relevant discipline such as Environmental Engineering, Sustainable Manufacturing, Industrial Ecology, Chemical or Process Engineering, Energy Systems, or a related field.

Our Successful Candidate

 

You will have a strong background in quantitative research and an interest in applying environmental and economic assessment methods to real-world industrial challenges.

 

You will demonstrate:

 

•    Experience in life cycle assessment, sustainability and techno-economic analysis.
•    Strong analytical skills with computational and numerical modelling experience.
•    Understanding of manufacturing, sustainability and resource efficiency.
•    Ability to evaluate technical data, assumptions and uncertainty.
•    Strong communication and collaboration skills.
•    Experience producing reports, publications and research outputs.

 

Experience with LCA software, process modelling, economic analysis tools or programming environments such as Python, MATLAB or R would be advantageous.

 

Knowledge of battery technologies, sustainable manufacturing, circular economy systems or industrial decarbonisation would also be desirable, although prior battery-specific research experience is not essential.

 

For informal enquiries, please contact Prof. Stephen Spooner – Stephen.Spooner@coventry.ac.uk

Our Mission

 

Coventry University Group is a global education group with a mission of Creating Better Futures. We are driven by our passionate belief in the transformational power of education and research to enable and empower our students, colleagues and partners and to improve the world around them. Our people are key to our success and each role contributes to the Group’s ongoing progress in communities around the world.

 

As an ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally.

The Role

 

We are seeking a Research Fellow in Data-Driven Materials Modelling and Process Optimisation to support the EPSRC-funded Data-Driven Control and Valorisation of Scrap Steel and Aluminium (DCVS) project. The role focuses on developing data-driven solutions to improve the quality, consistency and value of recycled metals by addressing challenges associated with variable scrap compositions and their impact on processing, alloy chemistry and final material performance.

 

In this role you will contribute to the development of computational and data-driven approaches to address these challenges, working particularly across the project's data analytics, modelling and process optimisation activities.

 

You will work closely with experimental researchers and industrial partners to develop, implement and validate models that link scrap material characteristics, processing conditions and resulting material quality.

 

This role will provide an opportunity to apply modern computational methods, including statistical modelling, machine learning, optimisation and physics-informed approaches, to challenging real-world problems in sustainable manufacturing.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

You will:

 

•    Develop and apply computational, statistical and machine learning models for recycled metals.
•    Analyse complex datasets to optimise processing, alloy control and material quality.
•    Quantify and manage uncertainty in scrap materials and manufacturing processes.
•    Build predictive tools, data workflows and reproducible analysis pipelines.
•    Validate models using experimental and industrial datasets.
•    Collaborate with industry partners to implement modelling solutions.
•    Contribute to publications, technical reports and project deliverables.

Qualifications Required

 

A PhD, or be close to completing one, in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Materials Science, Physics or a closely related discipline.

Our Successful Candidate

 

You will have proven experience in computational research, developing and evaluating numerical or data-driven models, with the ability to analyse complex datasets and apply appropriate analytical techniques to solve scientific and engineering challenges.

 

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

 

•    Machine learning, predictive analytics and statistical modelling.
•    Scientific programming in Python, MATLAB or similar environments.
•    Numerical modelling, simulation and computational materials science.
•    Mathematical optimisation, including constrained and multi-objective methods.
•    Uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis and probabilistic modelling.
•    Experimental and industrial data integration, processing and analysis.
•    Physics-informed, hybrid and digital twin modelling.
•    Manufacturing process, materials and industrial systems modelling.

 

You will have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate research questions into computational methodologies and deliver robust, well-documented technical outputs.

 

You will be comfortable working independently while collaborating with experimental researchers and industrial engineers from different technical backgrounds.

 

Previous experience in metallurgy, recycling or materials processing would be advantageous but is not essential. We particularly welcome candidates with strong computational skills who are interested in applying their expertise to sustainable manufacturing and industrial decarbonisation.

postings.advert_text:
A position exists, for a Research Associate in the Department of Engineering, to work on Energy Micropile Potential at urban scales.

The post-holder will lead the urban-scale modelling strand of EPSRC-funded project "UKRI-Norway: Energy Micropile Retrofits for Climate Change Adaptation of Existing Buildings", a collaboration between the Universities of Cambridge, Surrey, Leeds and NTNU. Positioned at the University of Cambridge and working with colleagues from all four organisations, the successful candidate will develop numerical and Machine Learning methods to quantify the potential of energy micropiles (EMPs) across urban environments in the UK and Norway. The methods will include assessment of geological suitability, structural health, and energy efficiency across existing building typologies under uncertain energy demand and climate change scenarios. The result will be (a) finding optimal heating and cooling regimes under structural health (b) identification and mapping of high-priority regions for EMP technologies and inform urban-scale deployment strategies under different energy demand and climate scenarios.

The post-holder will join the Energy Efficient Cities initiative (EECi) group at the Department of Engineering. They will generate high-impact publications and open datasets, contribute to future grant capture and industry partnerships, and support the training and mentoring of students and researchers within the Department of Engineering.

The post holder will be located in Department of Engineering, Trumpington Street, Cambridgeshire, UK.

The key responsibilities and duties are:

1) Develop large scale models to characterise EMP performance under varied climatic, geological and operational conditions.

2) Develop AI-driven surrogate models (e.g. artificial neural networks, Gaussian processes) to enable rapid design exploration and optimisation.

3) Translate modelling outcomes into practical design and operation guidelines and site-specific design tools.

4) Publish in leading journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to project meetings, reporting, progress updates, industry engagement, and knowledge exchange with partners.

The skills, qualifications and experience required to perform the role are expertise in modelling geothermal systems, independent thinking, and clarity in research communications.

Fixed-term: The funding is for 24 months or through until 31/03/2029, whichever comes soonest.

If you upload any additional documents which have not been requested, we will not be able to consider these as part of your application. Please submit your application by midnight on the closing date.

If you have any questions about this vacancy, please contact Professor Ruchi Choudhary, who is responsible for recruitment to this position, by email at rc488@cam.ac.uk.

Please quote reference NM51822 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

About the role

This is an excellent opportunity for a post-doctorate researcher (or equivalent) to build a research career in translational research that leverages on close collaborations between industry, clinicians, scientists and NIHR infrastructures. The post holder will be part of the core methodology team within the NIHR HealthTech Research Centre in In Vitro Diagnostics, contributing to a highly dynamic and multidisciplinary research programme focusing on evidence generation to further methodology research and to enable the design and development of health technologies, especially in-vitro diagnostics and medical devices for patients and the NHS. NIHR HRC IVD forms part of fourteen NIHR HealthTech Research centres across England.

Essential requirement includes a PhD (or equivalent) in Health Innovation Management, Health Technology Assessment, Translational Research Health Economics or a closely related discipline. Experiences working with industry or device manufacturers especially those utilising artificial intelligence/machine learning techniques are highly desirable. Both qualitative and quantitative research experiences are essential. This is a full-time post for 12 months in the first instance, based at the White City Campus, London.

The College is supportive of flexible working. The Department is happy to discuss the possibility of implementing such arrangements for this post, with suitably qualified people subject to operational arrangements.

What you would be doing

As a Health Technology Researcher at the NIHR HealthTech Research Centre in IVD, you will lead and contribute to research in health technology assessment, including health economic assessments, as well as methodology research, workforce development and training. Your work will inform healthcare decision-making and support the development, adoption, and funding of effective and efficient healthcare interventions.

Your work will include artificial intelligence and implementation science, complementing the qualitative and quantitative methodology research already employed within the HRC IVD core methodology team, also including human factors, health economics, stakeholder analysis, clinical pathway mapping, adoption studies, laboratory validation and market access. Working closely with clinicians, researchers, and policy stakeholders, you will develop and integrate multi-dimensional evidence into research studies, grant applications and publications.

Post doctorate-level training (or equivalent) in health technology assessment or a related discipline, with experience within a research environment in health, public health, or social care research.
Strong analytical skills, especially those utilising artificial intelligence/machine learning techniques, with practical experience in a broad range of techniques including interview, focus group, health economics.

Collaborative and multidisciplinary, with experience working with industry, clinicians and patients contributing to the health technology assessment across the research lifecycle.
Clear and effective communication skills, with the ability to translate complex evidence for academic, clinical, policy, and public audiences.
Experience contributing to NIHR or other competitively funded research, including involvement in study design, grant applications, and reporting.
Commitment to research quality, transparency, and governance, including adherence to NIHR, NICE, and other relevant methodological guidelines.

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.

Research Fellow in Additive Semiconductor Device Fabrication

The role

We seek a Research Fellow in Thin-Film Device and Circuit Fabrication to contribute to EPSRC project EP/Y000196/1. The appointment is part-time (0.5 FTE), with significant flexibility to adapt the working fraction and working pattern to the successful candidate's circumstances and the needs of the project. The post should start as soon as practicable and is expected to run until the end of July 2027.

The Researcher will undertake strongly experimental and data-intensive research on advanced multi-gate thin-film transistor structures. The work will involve fabrication using a variety of semiconductor and insulator materials, systematic electrical characterisation of large device arrays, automated measurement, and rapid analysis of device and circuit parameters. Particular emphasis will be placed on source-gated transistors (SGTs), multimodal transistors (MMTs), printing and dispensing processes, and rigorous extraction and interpretation of geometrical and electrical statistics.

About You

The successful candidate will have a PhD, or current progress towards a PhD, in Electronic Engineering or a closely related discipline with proven hands-on experience operating the XTPL Delta printer, including material selection, optimization of printing parameters for feature size and fill generation, remote operation, and maintenance routine. They will also have a deep understanding of the fabrication, operation, optimisation, and key performance indicators of source-gated transistors (SGTs) and multimodal transistors (MMTs). They would also have practical experience in thin-film device fabrication, including evaporation, dispensing, and printing, across relevant semiconductor and insulator material systems.

Additional Background Information

You will join a collaborative research team at the Advanced Technology Institute (ATI), University of Surrey, working on EPSRC project EP/Y000196/1. The role is strongly hands-on and data-intensive, with a particular emphasis on advanced thin-film transistor fabrication, automated characterisation, and rigorous analysis of large experimental datasets. Working with Dr Radu Sporea, you will interact closely with researchers and students contributing to related device, circuit, and technology-development activities.

Alongside the core experimental programme, the post holder will be expected to contribute to publication and presentation of research results, proposal development, and, where required, IP, commercialisation, technology transfer, and public engagement. Significant interaction with project partners is expected, and the role may involve national and international travel for collaborative experiments, analysis, and dissemination.

The University of Surrey is a research-intensive university based in Guildford. The Advanced Technology Institute is a multidisciplinary research environment spanning nanotechnology, energy, and large-area electronics, with specialist facilities supporting device fabrication and characterisation.

The University is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion. Research staff are supported in their career development through mentoring, training, and a collegial research environment in which varied skills and perspectives are valued.

Please contact Dr Sporea for all enquiries: r.a.sporea@surrey.ac.uk

Research Assistant (Robotics and Machine Learning) - FTC up to End of March 2027

The University of West London (UWL) is ranked as 41st in the UK in The Guardian University Guide 2026 and is the 1st London modern* university in The Times/The Sunday Times Good University Guide 2026. We are also ranked 2nd in London, 6th in England and 8th in the UK for overall student satisfaction in the National Student Survey 2026**. The UWL community is a diverse body of students and staff who work together to create an environment of success and achievement. We celebrate the diversity of our staff and promote our values in practice through our commitment to inclusivity, progression, and success.

The School

The School of Computing and Engineering (SCE) brings together expertise across computing, engineering and technology, with a strong focus on applied teaching, research and innovation.

The School supports research that addresses real-world technological challenges and works with external partners to translate research outcomes into practical applications.

This post will be based within the School's research environment, working with an academic project team on robotics, machine learning and cyber-security.

The project is supported by the University's research and innovation infrastructure and has a clear focus on developing and validating practical technology.

The successful candidate will contribute to a research project on independent monitoring of AI-driven industrial robots.

The Role 

We are seeking a motivated Research Assistant to join a research project developing an independent monitoring system that checks whether a robot has physically moved as it was commanded. The project focuses on AI-driven collaborative robots in industrial settings.

Working within the School of Computing and Engineering and under academic supervision, you will set up a collaborative robot arm with force/torque sensing and depth cameras, and adapt the monitoring software to contact-rich factory tasks such as insertion and fastening.

You will run a controlled test campaign in the laboratory, covering emulated cyber attacks, mechanical faults and AI errors, and build a labelled physical dataset from the results.

You will also benchmark the system against existing approaches and contribute to its testing, evaluation and documentation.

The role is hands-on and laboratory-based, with opportunities to contribute to project reports, technical demonstrations and engagement with industry partners.

This is a full-time, fixed-term appointment until 31 March 2027, based at the University of West London, with occasional travel to partner sites in the UK.

The Person

You will have a degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Machine Learning or a related subject, together with practical experience relevant to the role.

You will have strong Python skills and experience of applied machine learning, particularly for anomaly detection, behavioural analysis or time-series data.

Practical experience with robotics software such as ROS 2, and with sensors on a robot such as depth cameras or force/torque sensors, is essential.

You will have good analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work independently, manage tasks against project milestones and contribute effectively within a small research team.

Experience with contact-rich manipulation or Franka robot arms, security testing or fault injection, and awareness of industrial robot safety or cyber security standards would be desirable.

Funded Project - 29 Months

KTP Associate - Industrial AI and Process Optimisation Specialist (29-Month Knowledge Transfer Partnership) 
University of Wolverhampton & Vanguard Foundry Ltd.

This exciting Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) offers a unique opportunity to lead a transformational innovation project between the University of Wolverhampton and Vanguard Foundry Ltd, a leading UK manufacturer of iron castings and rapid prototyping solutions.

As the KTP Associate, you will drive the development of intelligent manufacturing systems that optimise sand reclamation, improve casting quality, reduce waste, and enhance sustainability. Working at the heart of a production foundry, you will establish advanced sensor networks, develop data-driven process controls, and create AI and machine learning solutions to monitor, predict and optimise manufacturing performance.

You will collaborate closely with University researchers, foundry specialists, suppliers and customers, gaining hands-on experience in industrial AI deployment while building an impressive research and innovation portfolio. The role combines data science, automation, materials engineering and sustainability, offering the opportunity to see your innovations directly implemented on the shop floor.

We are seeking candidates with an MSc or PhD in Engineering, Data Science, Computer Science, AI/ML, or a related discipline, alongside strong analytical, programming and problem-solving skills.

This is a practical, site-based role. A significant proportion of your time will be spent at the foundry: the sand plant, core shop, moulding lines and sand laboratory, working alongside operators, technicians and managers. Regular travel within the UK will be required, including between the foundry and the University of Wolverhampton, and to suppliers and other foundries around the UK. A full UK driving licence and the ability to drive to these sites would be a significant advantage.

In addition to the salary and development opportunities available through the KTP programme, the successful candidate may be eligible for a performance-related bonus linked to the successful achievement of project objectives and key milestones.

The Mathematical AI for Decision and Discovery (MADD) group at Lancaster University is recruiting postdoctoral researchers, funded by Dr Henry Moss’s UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship. These long-term posts run until November 2030 and come with a generous budget for conference travel and extended research visits to the group’s international collaborators.

About the role
In drug discovery, materials science and engineering design, every experiment is expensive. Bayesian optimisation and experimental design help choose which experiments to run, but they struggle when designs must meet complex, domain-specific feasibility requirements. MADD turns generative AI models, trained on known feasible designs, into rigorous decision rules for real experimental campaigns.

You will lead work in one or more of our research strands:

Gaussian process flows: probabilistic models that can be conditioned on almost any form of real-world knowledge, used as richer surrogates in experimental design.
Generative-AI-driven experimental design: theory and methods for Bayesian optimisation when candidates come from generative models.
Fine-grained control of generative models: steering pre-trained models to meet precise campaign criteria without costly retraining.

You will also publish at top venues; help shape the group’s open-source Python library; lead a flagship application with an industrial partner (e.g. drug discovery, protein engineering, fusion energy, sustainable aviation or hardware design); co-supervise PhD students; and mentor junior researchers.

These are full-time, fixed-term positions until November 2030. Flexible working arrangements will be considered, but you will be expected to be present on the Lancaster campus a minimum of two days per week.

What we’re looking for
A PhD in machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field, with a strong publication record in Bayesian optimisation, experimental design, Gaussian processes, probabilistic modelling, or deep generative modelling. We welcome both theory-focused candidates and those experienced in building large generative models. Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or JAX are expected.

We particularly welcome applications from women and other groups underrepresented in the mathematical sciences and AI.

Travel, visits and collaboration
External collaboration is at the heart of MADD. Each year you will receive funding for an extended research visit to a partner, attendance at major international conferences, regular visits to UK industrial partners, and external training.

Coventry University are recruiting a Research Fellow in Experimental Metallurgy and Materials Characterisation to join an exciting EPSRC-funded research project, Data-Driven Control and Valorisation of Scrap Steel and Aluminium (DCVS). The project brings together leading academic and industrial partners to develop new technologies and methodologies for improving the recovery, characterisation and reuse of recycled metals. By combining advanced material sensing, experimental metallurgy and data-driven process control, DCVS aims to enable greater use of secondary steel and aluminium in high-value manufacturing applications.

 

In this role you will play a central role in the experimental delivery of the project, developing and applying techniques to understand the chemical composition, processing behaviour and material properties of recycled metals.

 

Working alongside researchers, engineers and industrial partners, you will undertake practical research spanning scrap material assessment, Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), experimental melting and casting, and advanced materials characterisation.

 

Your research will generate the experimental evidence needed to validate new approaches to scrap assessment, material upgrading and process optimisation, directly supporting the development of predictive digital models within the wider project.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

 

•    Metal alloy development, melting, casting or solidification.
•    Optical spectroscopy or elemental analysis, including LIBS, XRF, OES or related techniques.

•    Recycling, secondary metallurgy or sustainable materials processing.

 

You will be organised, practical and comfortable working both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary research team. You should enjoy solving experimental challenges and have an interest in applying scientific research to real industrial problems.

The Role

 

Origin Tech and Newcastle University are recruiting a KTP Associate to lead a two-year Knowledge Transfer Partnership focused on improving Origin No Dig, a novel multi-award- winning product for repairing water pipeline leaks without excavation.

 

You will develop and validate computational models to understand how repair particles move through leaking pipes, accumulate at leaks and form an effective seal. Working with Origin’s engineering team and Newcastle University researchers, you will turn these findings into predictive tools and practical guidance for product development and deployment.

 

The role combines computational modelling, experimental validation and practical engineering, with the opportunity to take ownership of a project from initial investigation through to the real- world deployment of project deliverables.

 

About the Partnership 

 

Origin is a clean tech company based in Newcastle upon Tyne, delivering cutting-edge solutions for the Offshore, Nuclear, and Utilities sectors. They are one of the Sunday Times Top 100 fastest growing tech companies in the UK with a proven track record of success and exciting product innovations.

 

Their portfolio includes:

Origin Orbit® – combining satellite sensing, machine learning, and integrity expertise to provide vital insights for pipeline operators.
Origin No Dig® – a multi award-winning, patented technology that repairs water pipeline leaks without excavation.

 

You will work closely with Caitlin Woolley, Product Development Engineer at Origin Tech, and an interdisciplinary Newcastle University team led by Dr Weichao Shi and Dr Ben Wetenhall. The university team brings expertise in computational fluid dynamics, multiphase flow, porous media, fluid–structure interaction, pipeline engineering and data-driven engineering methods. You will have access to Newcastle University’s research facilities, including its specialist Marine Technology facilities, https://www.ncl.ac.uk/engineering/about-us/facilities/marine/.

 

A degree in Mechanical Engineering, Computational Engineering, Fluid Dynamics or a closely related discipline is essential. You will also work at Newcastle University and attend Origin Tech’s workshop and testing facility as required.

Your working week will be 40 hours per week. The shift pattern is Monday- Friday, 8 hours per day and there is flexibility within the core hours of 8:00AM-6:00PM.
Annual Leave applicable to this role 28 days plus bank holidays and one additional day off for your birthday.

Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department
Durham University’s Department of Archaeology is one of the UK’s best, with an outstanding reputation for excellence in teaching, research and employability of our students. We are regularly ranked one of the top three Archaeology departments in the UK (e.g. 2nd Research Excellence Framework [REF] 2021 and one of the top ten globally (5th in World University QS rankings 2026). Our expertise covers a broad chronological and geographical span, from the Palaeolithic to the present-day, and from East Asia to the Mediterranean, Europe and the British Isles. We have a strong research presence in Southwest Asia and the Eastern Mediterranean, that embraces fieldwork, landscapes, visual and material culture studies and bioarchaeology. We have a range of cutting-edge laboratories, including well-developed facilities for isotopic research, extensive commercial infrastructure, and a network of heritage-sector collaborators. The Department of Archaeology works closely with staff in two Durham University museums, the Oriental Museum and the Museum of Archaeology. For further information on our current projects, research and teaching see www.dur.ac.uk/archaeology

The Role

We are looking for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Landscape Archaeology to join our 3-year project ‘Aegean Unbound: revealing landscapes of Early Modernity’ (funded by the Leverhulme Trust). We will examine how ordinary communities adapted to changing political, economic, and environmental circumstances in the eastern Mediterranean between the 17th-19th centuries. By focusing on the exceptional but neglected evidence from historic landscapes around the Aegean, the project will integrate archaeology, archival research, and environmental studies to release new histories of these landscapes and their creators.
You will be a landscape archaeologist with a broad skill-set which includes archaeological fieldwork, GIS, spatial analysis and computer modelling. You will contribute throughout the three-year project and will be involved in key tasks for each case-study are including initial preparatory studies, landscape characterisation, fieldwork (including 3D recording of settlements and geoarchaeological sampling), analysis of survey and archive data; through to integration of results from geoarchaeological and environmental analyses, creation of landscape biographies with other team members, and preparing publications and other dissemination activities.
 

Key responsibilities:

To undertake desk-based analysis using GIS and field survey using digital tools relevant for landscape archaeology. 
To plan and manage delivery of research activities, including fieldwork.
To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include: research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To contribute to high quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines in consultation with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and to devise creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.
To engage in continuing professional development by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.   

This post is funded by the Aegean Unbound project, which sets out a fixed term 36 month position. The candidate would ideally be in place by January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

Successful applicants will, ideally, be in post by January 2027.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. The University closes between Christmas and New Year.

We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

If you have taken a career break or periods of leave that may have impacted on the volume and recency of your research outputs and other activities, such as maternity, adoption or parental leave, you may wish to disclose this in your application. The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role.

Professor Sam Turner, samuel.turner@durham.ac.uk

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk 

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. It will be at the discretion of the recruiting panel as to whether they will also consider any desirable criteria, but we would urge candidates to provide evidence for all criteria.  

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.

We prefer to receive applications online.   We will update you about your application at various points throughout the selection process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to make sure you have not missed any of our updates.

Short-listed candidates will be invited to the University, either virtually or in-person and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the Research Team.  The assessment for the post will normally include a presentation to staff and students in the Project Team followed by an interview and we anticipate that the assessments and interviews will take place over two days in or around December 2026. 

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date.

Job Description
 
Research Technician in Environmental Engineering and Microbiology  (Job Number: 26001523)
Department of Biosciences
Grade 6: - £31,861 to £32,722 per annum
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: 12 Months
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Closing Date: 08-Dec-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Not Applicable.
 

The University      

At Durham University we are proud of our people. A globally outstanding centre of educational excellence, a collegiate community of extraordinary people, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.    

Across the University we have a huge variety of roles and career opportunities, which together make us a large and successful community, which is a key hub of activity within our region and nationally.  Whether you are at the very start, middle or end of your career, there is a role for you. We believe everyone has their own unique skills to offer.    

We would be thrilled if you would consider joining our thriving University.  Further information about the University can be found here.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page.

The Role and the Department      

We are looking for a practical, well-organised Research Technician to join CARMA – the Co-selection of Antimicrobial Resistance by Metals Alliance. CARMA is a large, transdisciplinary UKRI-funded research programme investigating how metal pollution in rivers and wastewater co-selects for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and what this means for human health, environmental regulation and intervention. It brings together Durham University, Imperial College London, the University of Birmingham, the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi and Pondicherry University, with environmental engineers, microbiologists, infection specialists, modellers, economists, genomic experts, patients and practitioners.

The post is based in the Department of Biosciences at Durham, in the research group of Professor David Graham. You will carry out the project’s UK field sampling and much of the laboratory work that underpins it, working closely with the project’s Postdoctoral Research Associate in Environmental Engineering and Microbiology (the ‘PDRA’). Together with the PDRA you will collect river water and sediment from sites in North East England (including the North Tyne, South Tyne and Ouseburn) in wet and dry seasons. Back in the laboratory you will:

·         carry out water and sediment physicochemical analyses, including BOD, COD, nitrogen and phosphorus species, organic carbon, and total and bioavailable metals;

·         With the PDRA, culture, isolate and characterise antibiotic- and metal-resistant bacteria, including antimicrobial and metal susceptibility testing that complements whole-genome sequencing;

·         Extract, purify and quality-check DNA from bacterial isolates and from sediment and water samples, and prepare it for the different types of sequencing (short-read and long-read genome sequencing, and metagenomic sequencing), which will be carried out by specialist providers;

·         Prepare, store and ship samples for analysis of pharmaceuticals and antibiotic residues, which will be carried out by our partners in India;

·         Provide analytical support to colleagues in India, and help organise the shipping and processing of samples, isolates and DNA between and among project partners in the UK and India;

·         Give informal tutorials and guidance on laboratory methods to junior members of the laboratory, such as students.

Partners in India collect and analyse samples from the Ganges, Yamuna and near Chennai using the same protocols, so careful, consistent and well-documented work is central to the role. With samples, isolates and data moving between several laboratories in two countries, we are looking for someone who is exceptionally well organised. A full list of the analyses and techniques involved is given in the Annex at the end of this document. We do not expect applicants to have experience of all of them – training will be provided – but we ask you to tell us which you have and have not done.

The post reports to Professor David Graham and is co-managed by Dr Marcos Quintela-Baluja; day-to-day laboratory and field work will be planned and checked jointly with the PDRA. This is a laboratory- and field-based role, so you will normally work on site in Durham. Fieldwork involves working outdoors beside and in rivers in all weathers, sometimes with early starts, and we will discuss flexible working hours around field campaigns.

This post is full time and fixed term for 12 months, starting on 1 March 2027. There is the possibility of extension for up to a further 12 months, subject to the needs of the project, available funding and performance. The post is funded by a UKRI research grant (CARMA) and is tied to that time-limited project.

Working at Durham     

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

·         You’ll receive 27 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year - a total of 39 days. The University closes between Christmas and New Year. 

·         We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

·         No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

·         We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

·         We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

·         Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

·         Our family friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

·         We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

·         You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

·         Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

·         If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Our collective aim is to create an open and inclusive environment where everyone can reach their full potential, and we believe our staff should reflect the diversity of the global community in which we work.       

As a university equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key part of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do. We also live by our values and our Staff Code of Conduct. At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive. 

We welcome and encourage applications from members of groups who are under-represented in our work force including people with disabilities, women and black, Asian and minority ethnic communities. If you have taken time out of your career, and you feel it relevant, let us know about it in your application. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role.    

What you need to demonstrate when you apply/Person Specification  
  
When you apply it is important that you let us know what skills/experience you have from a similar role and/or what skills/experience you have which would make you right for this role. Further information about the role and responsibilities is at the end of this job description. Where a criteria has an asterisk* next to it, it may be given additional weighting when your application is considered.    
  
Your application should cover the following criteria:  

Essential Criteria

Qualifications/Experience

1.    Five GCSEs at least Grade C or level four (or equivalent) including English Language and Mathematics or a Post-16 qualification or equivalent experience. Also, a degree, HNC or HND in microbiology, biological or environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry or a related subject, or equivalent laboratory experience.

2.    Industry or professional knowledge/recognition relevant to the role supported by relevant courses or certification, for example training or certification in microbiology laboratory practice at Containment Level 2, analytical chemistry, or quality-assured laboratory methods.

3.    Experience of working in a team, for example in a research or analytical laboratory, or as part of a field sampling team.  

4.    Experience or ability to provide advice and guidance to a range of customers and colleagues, for example advising students, researchers or project partners on sampling or laboratory procedures  

5.    Experience of implementing policies and procedures, for example working to standard operating procedures (SOPs), quality-control requirements and sample chain-of-custody records.  

6.    Experienced practitioner who has led teaching/research projects working within an educational, commercial or industrial environment, for example taking responsibility for delivering a defined programme of laboratory analyses or a sampling campaign within a research project. 

7.    Extensive experience of relationship building and ability to turn opportunities into long-term knowledge exchange and collaboration, for example working with researchers, partner laboratories and analytical or sequencing service providers, including international partners.

8.    Extensive knowledge and experience of monitoring your activities and others to ensure health and safety regulations are adhered to, including laboratory (COSHH, Containment Level 2 microbiology) and fieldwork (working beside and in rivers) risk assessment.  

9.    Hands-on experience of culture-based microbiology, including aseptic technique, selective plating, isolation of pure cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. *

10.  Hands-on experience of water and/or sediment chemistry analysis (e.g. BOD, COD, nutrients, organic carbon or metals). *

11.  Experience of extracting DNA, and assessing its quality, from bacterial cultures and/or environmental samples. *

12.  Willingness to carry out regular outdoor field sampling beside and in UK rivers in all seasons.

13.  A full driving licence valid in the UK, as field sites are in rural Northumberland and Tyneside. *

Skills/Abilities/Knowledge

14.  Good spoken and written communication skills including the ability to develop effective working relationships, both internally and externally, including with project partners in India.

15.  Strong digital competence across a range of digital devices and apps including Microsoft 365 (especially Excel and Teams), shared online data platforms and laboratory instrument software.

16.  Committed to continuing professional development.

17.  Regulatory, local and national professional knowledge and experience of compliance, for example COSHH, the handling of biological agents, and the regulations for packaging and shipping biological and environmental samples (e.g. UN3373). 

18.  Ability to solve problems and decide on and plan appropriate solutions, for example troubleshooting failed analyses, quality-control failures or field logistics.

19.  Professional knowledge and expertise in one or more areas of technical specialism, and the application of skills to create, build, construct and realise new and innovative resources, equipment and research outputs, here, environmental microbiology and/or water and sediment chemistry.

20.  Demonstrable ability to deliver high precision technical skills and the operation of standard and complex scientific, technical and creative equipment, for example spectrophotometers, pH/DO/conductivity meters, digestion units, biosafety cabinets, centrifuges and DNA quantification instruments.

21.  Exceptional organisational skills and attention to detail, including accurate record-keeping, sample tracking, data entry and coordinating sample shipments between laboratories. *

22.  Ability to explain laboratory methods clearly and to give informal tutorials to students and junior colleagues.

23.  Ability to work both independently and as part of a small team to meet sampling and analytical deadlines.

Desirable Criteria 

24.  Research experience in antimicrobial resistance or environmental microbiology, including work with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing or carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales.

25.  Experience of determining minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) by broth microdilution to EUCAST or CLSI standards, and/or of metal susceptibility testing.

26.  Experience of operating ICP-OES/ICP-MS, a TOC analyser or ion chromatography.

27.  Experience of extracting metagenomic DNA from sediments, soils or water, and of preparing DNA for short-read and long-read sequencing.

28.  Experience of carrying out sequencing yourself (e.g. Illumina library preparation, or running Oxford Nanopore sequencing).

29.  Experience of preparing samples for trace organic analysis (e.g. solid-phase extraction of pharmaceuticals).

30.  Experience of packing and shipping biological or environmental samples, including internationally. 

31.  Experience of working in international or multidisciplinary research teams

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification above. Where there are desirable criteria we would also urge you to provide any relevant evidence. Please don’t forget to check if there is any weighted criteria (see above).      

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.        

Submitting your application       

We prefer to receive applications online. We will update you about your application at various points during the process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to ensure you receive all emails        

What you are required to submit:   

Your CV    
A covering letter or statement which shows examples of how you meet all of the essential criteria within the Person Specification of the job description. With particular emphasis on hands-on field sampling, culture-based microbiology, water and sediment chemistry, and DNA extraction.
A completed copy of the analysis checklist in the Annex (or an equivalent list in your statement) showing, for each technique (A1–F1), whether you have performed it independently (I), under supervision (S) or not yet (N). This helps us plan training; we do not expect any applicant to have done everything on the list.     

Next steps

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview, in person or online, lasting approximately 45 minutes. This will include a discussion of your practical experience against the Annex checklist and, for in-person interviews, a short tour of the laboratories. We anticipate that interviews will take place in January 2027 [date to be confirmed].

Contact details       

If you would like to have a chat or ask any questions about the role, Professor David Graham (david.w.graham@durham.ac.uk) or Dr Marcos Quintela-Baluja (marcos.quintela-baluja@durham.ac.uk) would be happy to speak to you.

About the role

Help stem the flood of AI-accelerated research fabrication as a Research Associate.

Fraudulent publications are a massive problem for the scientific record. Thanks in part to forensic metascience or “science sleuths”, new infrastructures for fraud detection are slowly being developed and implemented. Yet with generative AI, we are bound to see a step change in the quantity and quality of research fabrication that risks overwhelming scientific quality control and correction mechanisms. Funded by an ESRC Metascience research grant, the 18-month project “After the Flood” will develop an anticipatory taxonomy and scenarios of AI threats to scientific integrity over the next 5 years, map existing sleuthing practices that could be implemented in agentic workflows, and co-create a policy and R&D roadmap of desirable, effective, and equitable sociotechnical countermeasures to AI-assisted scientific fraud.

The project brings together experts in AI-based scientific workflows (Prof Sam Cooper) and futures methods (Dr Leila Sheldrick) at Imperial College London with leading forensic metascientists at the University of Bern (Dr Ian Hussey, co-creator of INSPECT-SR). It will work closely with the International Science Council to ensure our work reaches science organisations world-wide and is inclusive of global, and research technology provider Digital Science.

What you would be doing

We are looking for someone interested in telling stories about the future, by developing rigorous and participatory visions that will shape policy and practice.  

You will take ownership of the futures research components of the project, working in close collaboration with the investigators and a research associate in forensic metascience at the University of Bern. Under supervision of Strategic Futures Lab lead Dr Leila Sheldrick, you will conduct horizon scanning of relevant information and recruit and work with members of different scientific stakeholder groups through an online Delphi, co-design, and back-casting workshops. This will include engaging with scientific publishers, researchers and research integrity specialists, funders and policy-makers, and AI/technology developers. You will conduct red-teaming workshops with AI researchers and forensic meta-scientists to safely assess research fabrication capabilities of current agentic workflows. You will synthesise results into scenarios and policy and R&D roadmaps for a desirable science future.

What we are looking for

A PhD in a relevant field (e.g., futures studies, qualitative social research, science and technology studies, design research, innovation studies), or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience
Practical experience in applying futures methods (e.g., horizon scanning, weak-signal logging, scenario development, backcasting)
Practical experience in conducting online and in-person participatory/co-design stakeholder workshops
Practical experience in qualitative study design, data collection, and analysis 
A strong publication track record in relevant venues, commensurate with career stage
Experience of interacting with policy-makers and senior officials and professionals in institutions
Experience producing polished visual and audiovisual research deliverables for wider stakeholder circles, such as white papers, project brochures, keynote presentation
Experience working with current generative AI services and agentic workflows across the research pipeline
Practical experience in conducting online Delphis  
Experience in collaborating with technical and engineering researchers

What we can offer you

The opportunity to directly inform science policy and systems globally on an urgent issue
Active mentorship and dedicated time for career development, including support for fellowship and follow-on grant applications
Engagement opportunities spanning general public, press, and industry stakeholders

Further information

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week).

This role is for a fixed-term contract for 12 months.

About Us

The School of Cardiovascular and Metabolic Medicine & Sciences (SCMMS) is one of the UK's leading centres for cardiovascular, metabolic and translational research. As part of the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine at King's College London, the School brings together internationally renowned researchers, clinicians and educators to advance understanding of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity and related disorders, with the aim of improving prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

SCMMS is recognised for its excellence in both research and education, delivering high-quality undergraduate and postgraduate programmes that provide students with access to cutting-edge scientific discoveries, innovative teaching and world-class clinical expertise. The School maintains strong partnerships with NHS organisations, research institutes and industry collaborators, creating an environment that supports scientific innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration and real-world impact.

The School comprises more than 65 academic research groups, over 400 staff and approximately 110 PhD students across King's College London's Guy's, St Thomas' and Denmark Hill campuses. Researchers benefit from access to state-of-the-art facilities and specialist expertise, including high-throughput screening, multimodality in vivo imaging, proteomics, integrative physiology, and viral and non-viral vector production.

As part of King's Health Partners, SCMMS provides an outstanding environment for translational research and basic-clinical collaboration. The School has a strong commitment to mentoring, career development and fostering an inclusive and supportive community in which staff and students can thrive 

About The Role

We are seeking a Research Assistant to join Professor Afshan Malik’s research group at King’s College London. Our research focuses on understanding the role of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and mitochondrial dysfunction in metabolic disease, with a particular interest in obesity and diabetes.

The post holder will primarily contribute to PAS GRAS, a European collaborative research programme investigating metabolic, environmental and behavioural determinants of obesity in children, adolescents and young adults. King’s is the UK partner in a consortium involving researchers across Europe, and the successful candidate will support the delivery of defined PAS GRAS activities, milestones and research outputs.

The role will combine laboratory and data-based research. Key activities will include measurement of mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) using qPCR and analysis of mtDNA-CN alongside metabolic and selected proteomic biomarkers. The Research Assistant will also undertake training in the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform and contribute to statistical and bioinformatic analyses of large-cohort data. Where required, they will support laboratory studies using established molecular and cellular techniques. Appropriate training will be provided for methods and analytical platforms where needed.

The post holder will contribute to the wider activities of the PAS GRAS consortium through preparation of research reports, presentations, scientific manuscripts and dissemination materials, and participation in project and research-group meetings. They will also contribute to the day-to-day organisation of the Malik laboratory, including maintenance of laboratory and sample records and routine laboratory activities.

The successful candidate will have a BSc and/or MSc in a relevant biomedical or life-science discipline, relevant laboratory research experience, and an interest in mitochondrial biology, obesity or metabolic disease. Strong organisational, data-analysis, communication and collaborative working skills are important. The post holder will be responsible to Professor Afshan Malik and will work closely with members of the Malik laboratory and PAS GRAS collaborators.

This is a part-time post (80% FTE, 28 hours per week), and you will be offered a  fixed term contract for 15 months from the start date.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Good undergraduate and/or Master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g. cell/molecular biology, biochemistry or life/biological sciences).
Proven experience of working in a scientific laboratory.
Strong background in Cell/Molecular biology.
Mammalian cell culture and/or qPCR experience.
Reliable, motivated and hard-working.
Able to plan and prioritise workload and keep clear and well-organised laboratory notes and records.
Good communication and writing skills.

Desirable criteria

Research experience in related field (e.g setting up cellular, molecular and/or biochemical assays, cell imaging etc).
Experience/interest in mitochondria/obesity/diabetes.
Demonstrated ability to work as part of a team and undertake share of group tasks.
Experience of contributing to reports and articles for publication.

Role Description

Department of Psychology

The York Episodic Memory Lab, led by Dr Aidan Horner, at The Department of Psychology, University of York, is seeking a postdoctoral research associate to work for 10 months. The role will work on a Leverhulme Trust funded project on “Boosting long-term memory via environmental structure in virtual reality". The goal of the project is to understand how our spatial environment shapes learning, and how we can structure our environment to boost learning. The project will use experimental psychology, computational modelling, and virtual reality environments. The candidate will have a strong track record in the psychology and cognitive neuroscience of memory. They will have experience in developing experimental psychology tasks and applying them to questions related to memory.

 You must have a PhD and first degree in psychology or a related discipline and postdoctoral experience in relation to episodic memory.

Knowledge of experimental psychology and of psychological research techniques are essential.

You should have experience of independent and collaborative research, and of writing up research for publication.

You should have good attention to detail, commitment to high quality research, a collaborative ethos, and enthusiasm for the research area and project.
